title: AiCallRecordedPayload
description: ai.call.recorded v1 (plan L40, one AI meter across the network). One AI call, wherever it happened: OpenVibe.AI's own runs, a harness turn in Codes, an Actor task, Vibe, a local model on a person's own machine. who and where: subject (the person, or null when the call is anonymous), attribution (the site or app the call came from, free text such as 'site:design'), surface (the product surface, free text such as 'design.generate' or 'codes.turn'). what ran: system (ai, harness:claude-code, harness:codex, actor, node), provider, model, effort. who paid: paid_by (own_key, openvibe_key, plan, own_machine, free_tier, network_allowance, org_key) and paid_by_detail (for example 'anthropic ...a1b2' for a person's own key, or 'claude-max' for a plan). tokens: input (the UNCACHED input tokens), output, reasoning, cache_read, cache_write (with cache_write_ttl 5m or 1h), images, audio_seconds, video_seconds. money, in USD: list_cost_usd (what the tokens cost at the human-typed list prices), charged_usd (what the payer was actually charged), fee_usd (the network's fee on top), cache_saved_usd (what the cache saved against the plain input price). price_source says where the prices came from ('models', 'pricing', 'flat', or 'no cache price' when no cache price is typed and the cache tokens are priced at the input price), price_date the day the price was checked. how it went: latency_ms, ttft_ms, attempts, outcome. ids: run_id or turn_id, and at. The record carries NO prompt and NO answer text, ever. A ledger (OpenVibe.AI) rolls the records up; a record consumed twice is stored once (idempotent by system and run_id or turn_id). Envelope: subject { type: run, id: <run_id> } or { type: user, id: <subject> }, visibility internal, priority low, actor service:ai. Since 1.1.0 (ai-metrics.md): OPERATION, STREAMED, TPS, QUEUE_MS, TASK, TASK_ID, TASK_MS, HARNESS, PLACE, ERROR_CLASS, FALLBACKS, CACHE_HIT, TOOL_CALLS and REGION, all optional. Products other than AI send their calls to POST /api/v1/usage/calls (ai.call-report@1); AI prices and publishes them.

subject.description: The person the call was made for, or null when the call was anonymous.

attribution.description: The site or app the call came from, as '<type>:<id>' (for example 'site:design'), empty when nothing is known.

surface.description: The product surface: 'design.generate', 'codes.turn', 'ai.generate'. Free text, so a new surface needs no new contract.

effort.description: The reasoning effort the call asked for, when it asked for one.

paid_by_detail.description: Which key or plan paid, for example 'anthropic ...a1b2' or 'claude-max'. Never a whole secret.

input.description: The uncached input tokens. Cache reads and cache writes are counted on their own fields.

cache_write_ttl.description: How long the written cache entry lives, when the provider says.

list_cost_usd.description: What the tokens cost at the human-typed list prices.

charged_usd.description: What the payer was actually charged. A person's own key is never charged here: 0.

fee_usd.description: The network's fee on top of the cost, when the OpenVibe key paid.

cache_saved_usd.description: What the cached tokens saved against the plain input price.

price_source.description: Where the prices came from: 'models' (a person's typed model row), 'pricing' (AI_PRICING_JSON), 'flat' (the flat rates), 'no cache price' (no cache price is typed, so the cache tokens are priced at the input price).

price_date.description: The day the price was checked, when it was.

ttft_ms.description: Time to the first token, when the call streamed and it was measured.

operation.description: Since 1.1.0: what kind of call it was.

streamed.description: Since 1.1.0: whether the answer came as a stream (TTFT is only measured on one).

tps.description: Since 1.1.0: output tokens per second after the first token (decode speed); null when not streamed or too short to measure.

queue_ms.description: Since 1.1.0: time waiting before the call was sent (a queue, a rate gate).

task.description: Since 1.1.0: the task kind the call served (a task name, a workflow key, chat.reply, code.turn).

task_id.description: Since 1.1.0: the task or run this call is one step of, so cost and time add up per task.

task_ms.description: Since 1.1.0: on the last call of a task, the whole task’s wall time.

harness.description: Since 1.1.0: the harness that made the call (openvibe, dsh, codex, claude-code, gemini-cli, opencode …).

place.description: Since 1.1.0: where the model ran: a provider’s API, the person’s own machine, a community machine, a signed-in plan, OpenVibe’s own hosts.

error_class.description: Since 1.1.0: on a failure, its class (rate_limited, timeout, context_length, refused, auth, server, network, invalid).

fallbacks.description: Since 1.1.0: how many offers failed before the one that answered.

cache_hit.description: Since 1.1.0: true when the whole answer came from OpenVibe’s exact answer cache (no model ran).

tool_calls.description: Since 1.1.0: tool calls the model asked for in this call.

region.description: Since 1.1.0: the provider region or data centre, when known.
